note: Oracle for forge's end-to-end vs to-the-boundary classification (§9, issue #17). Hand-derived (R-CHAR-3). The classification is SYNTACTIC (a transitive-call-closure analysis on the parsed Program), orthogonal to a fn's verification level. END-TO-END iff the fn's closure reaches no #[boundary] and no #[slag] fn; otherwise TO-THE-BOUNDARY via the reached crossing. Boundary syntax requires #16 (shipped). Expected per-fn scope is hand-derived from the call graph.

end_to_end.name: corpus_sum
end_to_end.why: sum calls only spec_sum (a spec fn, pure) -> closure reaches no boundary/slag -> END-TO-END.

end_to_end.name: corpus_binary_search
end_to_end.why: binary_search calls only registry combinators (pure) -> END-TO-END.

to_boundary.name: direct_boundary_caller
to_boundary.program: #[boundary("ext::ext_id")] fn ext_id(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure ; fn caller(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure { ext_id(x) }
to_boundary.why: caller's body calls ext_id (a #[boundary] fn, foreign unproven body) -> caller is TO-THE-BOUNDARY via ext_id. (caller may itself be L3-proved against ext_id's contract — scope is orthogonal to level.)

to_boundary.name: transitive_boundary_caller
to_boundary.program: #[boundary("ext::ext_id")] fn ext_id(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure ; fn g(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure { ext_id(x) } fn h(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure { g(x) }
to_boundary.why: h -> g -> ext_id: the transitive closure of h reaches the boundary -> h is TO-THE-BOUNDARY (transitive, via ext_id).

to_boundary.name: slag_caller
to_boundary.program: #[slag(reason = "hand-tuned", owner = "agent:x", review = "required")] fn vendored(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure { x } fn caller(x: u32) -> u32 req x < 100 ens result == x fx pure { vendored(x) }
to_boundary.why: caller calls vendored (a #[slag] fn, trusted-by-fiat body) -> caller is TO-THE-BOUNDARY via vendored (slag is in the closure).
